A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same federated Granger causality framework and contain complete main texts and Appendices A.1–A.9. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables and appendices without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations on HAI and SWaT, including learned causal matrices, robustness losses, scalability results and communication savings in Sections 8–9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original synthetic and HAI/SWaT experimental results in Sections 8–9, Tables 3–7 and Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: The Kalman-filter clients, linear additive augmentation, server model, losses and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Equation (2) substitutes the measurement transpose for the augmentation derivative, making the existing update explicit rather than changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic state-space systems and the HAI and SWaT industrial-control datasets. The perturbation, topology-change and scalability scenarios are retained without additions or removals.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same three comparison variants: no client augmentation, no server model and pre-trained clients. The centralized oracle and centralized estimation comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The synthetic defaults of two clients, measurement dimension 8 and state dimension 2 are retained, as are the perturbation levels and topology tests. Section 9 retains the correlation threshold, SVD/VAR preprocessing, nominal-data training and centralized-reference evaluation.

E4.justification: The component ablations and causality-perturbation/topology tests in Table 4, scalability studies in Table 5 and convergence analyses in Figure 2 are unchanged. No additional robustness test, sensitivity analysis or case study appears.

E5.justification: Run counts and seeds remain unspecified. Figure 3 retains identical shaded curves without a newly supplied explanation of their statistical construction, and neither version adds confidence-interval definitions or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 3–5 and 7 retain identical numerical results, and Figures 2–3 contain identical plot images. For example, Table 7 reports the same Frobenius errors of 0.8140 for HAI and 3.0816 for SWaT, with 144 and 176 bytes saved per communication round.

T1.justification: The mathematical results and proof arguments are retained. Theorem 5.4 makes its existing per-client formulation explicit, while Equations (13)–(17) receive index cleanups. The added homogeneous Gaussian noise statement in Appendix A.6 repeats the covariance qI assumption already stated in v1's proof and two-client setup; it introduces no new assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about federated causality learning, convergence, oracle approximation, differential privacy, robustness and scalability. No core contribution is added, removed or strengthened.

C2.justification: The experimental interpretations and Appendices A.7–A.9 retain the same explanations, unresolved observations and limitations. These include possible false alarms, possible pre-training overfitting, linearity and temporal restrictions, and synchronous participation assumptions.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds a repository address for the paper's code and associated experiments; v1 supplies pseudocode but no corresponding code-access statement. Other implementation information is unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including distinctions from vertical federated learning, split learning, centralized Granger causality and distributed Kalman filtering. Bibliography entries move across pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 revises the author/affiliation presentation, changes the conference header from Accepted to Published, adds acknowledgments and makes limited wording and mathematical-exposition edits. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block changes from separate institutional columns to a compact shared listing. Acknowledgments and local spacing changes reflow references and appendix pages, and Figure 3 shifts slightly. Figure content, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation through the new code-access pointer in Section 3 and clearer presentation of existing gradients, indices and noise assumptions. The method, experimental evidence and theoretical substance remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited. Actual code availability and reproducibility cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.
